name: Hey Product Page Banner support-rescue alternative
demand: Weak evidence for the rescue feature. Shopify reports millions of merchants in 175+ countries, but the exact count, relevant store population and search volume for this problem are unverified: https://www.shopify.com/investors. Store Leads estimated Hey at 125 installed stores on 2026-07-31, down 34.2% year over year; Shopify’s listing has 32 reviews as of this check. The install figure is a third-party estimate, not Shopify-confirmed usage: https://storeleads.app/reports/shopify/app/product-page-descriptions-hey https://apps.shopify.com/product-page-descriptions-hey. A broader labels-and-badges analogue, DECO, had tracker estimates of 8,487 stores on 2026-10-02 and 8,587 on 2026-10-14; its Shopify listing shows 1,735 reviews. These indicate adjacent feature demand, not demand for monitoring or repair: https://storeleads.app/reports/shopify/app/product-labels https://www.storecensus.com/shopify-stores-using/product-labels https://apps.shopify.com/product-labels. Demand for the proposed health monitoring and self-serve fixes is unverified.
prices: Hey: free for stores with up to 3 products, $4.99/month or $49.99/year: https://apps.shopify.com/product-page-descriptions-hey. Direct new entrant Dynamic Product Banners: free for up to 3 product-page blocks, then $4.99/month or $49.99/year: https://apps.shopify.com/dynamic-product-banners. Product Page Banners & Text: $4.95/month, or $19.95/month for Shopify Plus: https://apps.shopify.com/product-page-badges. DECO: free tier, then $9, $19 and $39/month: https://apps.shopify.com/product-labels. These are listed prices, not proof of paid customers or revenue.
copy_speed: High for the widget itself. Shopify lists Dynamic Product Banners as launched 2026-04-01; it offers product-page messaging, theme blocks, targeting and scheduling, but had 0 reviews on the listing when checked: https://apps.shopify.com/dynamic-product-banners. Store-Tip Emergency Banner launched 2026-08-14 at $4.99/month, but is a general announcement banner rather than a product-page health monitor: https://apps.shopify.com/emergency-banner. A creator announced Aplo, an adjacent product-page content builder, as newly launched on 2026-10-20; that date comes from the creator’s post, not an independently verified App Store launch record: https://www.reddit.com/r/ShopifyAppMarketing/comments/1xaz215/i_built_a_nocode_a_content_app_for_shopify/. I found no verified launch of an equivalent monitoring-and-repair product; that absence is not exhaustive research.
platform_risk: High platform dependence; medium-to-high native-feature risk. Shopify says theme app blocks need compatible sections and merchants add them through the theme editor; switching the published theme can require reactivating apps: https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-store/themes/customizing-themes/apps. Shopify’s app API exposes extension activation status, but that data comes from the published theme only: https://shopify.dev/docs/api/app-home/latest/apis/authentication-and-data/app-api. Shopify requires theme app extensions for theme-modifying apps, rather than direct theme-code changes: https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/shopify-app-store/app-store-requirements. This limits automatic repair of arbitrary theme or third-party app code; a realistic repair may need to guide the merchant to activate or reposition the app block. Shopify announced Canvas with Sidekick on 2026-10-01; Canvas did not support app blocks or embeds at launch, but native AI theme editing creates longer-term pressure on basic widgets: https://changelog.shopify.com/posts/design-a-fully-bespoke-store-with-canvas https://www.shopify.com/news/introducing-canvas.
defensible_asset: No current moat evidenced. A possible future asset is a consented, aggregated compatibility and repair dataset by theme/version, with verified outcomes. That is a hypothesis, not an existing advantage; no UK-exclusive or regulated data is apparent from the proposed feature, and a simple banner has low apparent switching cost. Shopify’s extension API offers activation-status data for the published theme, not a ready-made cross-store repair dataset: https://shopify.dev/docs/api/app-home/latest/apis/authentication-and-data/app-api.
build_effort: Unverified estimate. A basic banner using a theme app extension is a conventional Shopify app component; a reliable monitor adds installation and activation checks, storefront health checks, alerts and guided recovery. Cross-theme automatic repair is substantially harder and constrained by Shopify’s extension rules and published-theme-only activation data. Shopify’s extension configuration and App Store requirements describe the implementation and review constraints: https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/online-store/theme-app-extensions/configuration https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/shopify-app-store/app-store-requirements. Treat any delivery timeline as unverified until scoped against a chosen repair workflow.
channel: Use inbound Shopify App Store discovery, search-oriented troubleshooting content and transparent public posts that invite opt-in interest. Avoid unsolicited email, SMS, WhatsApp and social DMs to individuals or sole traders: ICO guidance includes stored social-media direct messages as electronic mail and treats sole traders as individual subscribers, for whom consent or the soft opt-in is generally required. The ICO says its guidance is under review following the Data (Use and Access) Act: https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/ https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guide-to-pecr/electronic-and-telephone-marketing/electronic-mail-marketing/.
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified. The <=5 h/week constraint is not evidenced by a live product or support data. Automated onboarding, activation checks, alerting and first-line help are plausible; theme-specific exceptions and app support still need measurement.
desk_test: Within one day, make a one-page mock showing healthy, inactive-block and compatibility-warning states. Manually review the visible 2025–26 reviews for Hey and its closest banner alternatives, separating unresolved compatibility/support reports from resolved incidents. Then post one transparent, opt-in question with the mock in a relevant Shopify merchant or developer community where promotion is allowed; ask for recent examples and whether merchants would install at the existing $4.99/month market price. Do not cold-message respondents. Advance only if unrelated merchants describe recent recurring failures and request access at a stated price; otherwise keep the idea at desk-test stage.
red_flags: The supplied June 12, 2025 outage review was edited on June 26, 2025 to say the issue was fixed, so it is weak evidence of a continuing gap: https://apps.shopify.com/product-page-descriptions-hey. A separate listing search result shows a March 3, 2026 review alleging no support response, but this remains one self-reported incident, not verified system failure: https://apps.shopify.com/product-page-descriptions-hey. Hey’s estimated installs were declining in the July 2026 tracker snapshot. No qualifying revenue proof or paid-user count was found; listed subscription prices and review totals do not establish sales. The new direct competitor already offers the basic widget at the same $4.99/month price. Automation share is 0% verified because the proposed product is not running; >=50% automation and <=5 h/week remain unproven. Verdict: desk-test only; do not treat the lead as meeting the owner constraints yet.
